title: Impact of Thermal Processing vs. High Pressure on Blueberries
metaDescription: We look at a scientific study on how thermal processing and ultra-high pressure affect anthocyanin profiles in blueberry juice.
excerpt: A recent scientific study analyzed how thermal processing and ultra-high pressure affect the properties of blueberry juice.
imageAlt: Fresh blueberry juice in a glass next to whole blueberries on a wooden table.

blocks.text: Introduction: processing methods in blueberry juice

When we consume blueberries in liquid form, the method used to process the food plays a fundamental role in its final composition. In food science, understanding how different technologies alter the natural compounds of the fruit is a subject of constant research. Recently, a study published in the scientific literature addressed this topic to better understand what happens at the molecular level when we make blueberry juice under different technical conditions.
What the source says about thermal processing and high pressure

The scientific research compared two main methods applied to blueberry juice: thermal processing (TP, at 85 °C for 30 minutes) and ultra-high pressure processing (UHP, between 300 and 600 MPa for 5 to 15 minutes). The authors evaluated the impacts of both techniques on anthocyanin profiles and the overall metabolic composition of the juice.

The results showed that thermal processing produced significantly higher contents of total anthocyanins, flavonoids and phenolic compounds, as well as higher antioxidant activity compared with ultra-high pressure. Targeted metabolomic analysis indicated that, under thermal processing, three anthocyanin monomers and five proanthocyanidins increased between 19% and 181%, while three cyanidin-type monomers decreased between 17% and 20%. This suggests a simultaneous process of release and degradation. On the other hand, ultra-high pressure produced smaller metabolic changes and kept the anthocyanin species practically unaltered, reflecting a gentler, non-thermal disruption.
Context: the behavior of blueberry compounds

These findings provide specific information on the stability of the bioactive compounds present in wild and cultivated berries. Anthocyanins are known to be the pigments responsible for the characteristic coloring of blueberries and to have high antioxidant capacity. The study shows that applying heat can facilitate the release of these compounds from the fruit’s cellular structures, although it can also induce the degradation of certain specific monomers. In contrast, non-thermal technologies such as ultra-high pressure seek to preserve the native profile of the raw material more faithfully without resorting to high temperatures.
What it means for you in daily practice

From a practical perspective, this kind of scientific research offers useful guidance for the food industry when choosing technologies that maximize the presence of desirable compounds in commercial juices. For those of us who enjoy blueberries at home, whether in fresh or processed preparations, understanding that each handling method subtly alters the fruit’s chemistry reminds us of the importance of valuing both fresh options and those made through controlled processes that care for the nutritional quality of food.
The study shows that processing techniques directly influence the chemistry of blueberry juice. At Fresh Pick we follow science closely to give you rigorous information about this wonderful fruit.
